With the deck and steps added in a temp copy, the room check says OK: 27 of 28 floor cells reachable (the 28th is the barrel), min light 9, 0 dark cells, FIT OK.

waste.what: Verifying the room in a temp copy: the room check reads the floor from the deck at y 2, which the fittings part (P4) has not built yet, so I wrote a throwaway script that adds the deck and steps to a copy of build.nbt before running the check.
waste.cost: one script, one extra make and check cycle (about 2 minutes)
waste.tool: room check or plan should take a flag such as --assume-deck (or read the porch deck from plan.md's porch_run spec) so a room can be checked before the porch part is merged

waste.what: Writing the layers() legend and three layers by hand for a 10 x 3 porch, with the cell-by-cell counting of the character columns.
waste.cost: about 4 minutes of drafting and recounting cells
waste.tool: plan.md-driven plan output that already includes the furniture-free grid as an editable layers() block, or a plan --draw flag printing the x-mod-10 ruler for the full width of the room

waste.what: Trying to place a hanging lantern under the porch beam: I had to fall back to standing lanterns on fence posts because nothing is built at y 6 yet, and I only found this by reading the room light map.
waste.tool: room check should report which cells lack a ceiling block (the hanging_lantern spot), so the hanging option can be chosen before building

companions.task: hang the swing bench from the porch beam at y 6 (chains at x 86 and 87, seat at y 4), and build the porch beam and deck that the swing and rockers stand on, so the swing is grounded in the real build instead of floating.
confirm the standing lanterns on the corner fence posts and the barrel lamp against the final porch ceiling, and move one to a hanging lantern under the beam if the beam is solid where I need it.

left: Floating-group warnings in `mcd check build.nbt` (rockers, swing chains and seat, barrel and lamps: 3 groups) clear only after the fittings part lays the porch deck (y 2) and porch beam (y 6, x 85..94 z 7).

The real build.nbt room check says NEEDS WORK (no walk into the room) until the fittings part builds the deck and the front steps at x 88..91 z 6; with those in place it says OK (tested in a temp copy).
Swing chains at x 86..87 z 7 hang from the porch beam at y 6, which fittings must build; if the beam is absent the swing is floating.

plan.md and elements.md have no porch-specific checkbox for this room, so no ticks were changed.

structured_output.summary:
Bungalow porch (x 85..94, y 3..5, z 7..9) furnished: swing bench on the front bay (chains hung from the porch beam), two rockers facing the lane, a barrel side table with a lamp, and standing lanterns on fence posts at the corners; the x 89 z 7..9 lane to the door stays clear. make.sh produced a whole build.nbt with 12 cells placed by this part, no REFUSED or OFF-PALETTE lines.
With the deck and steps added in a temp copy, the room check says OK: 27 of 28 floor cells reachable (the 28th is the barrel), min light 9, 0 dark cells, FIT OK.
The real build.nbt room check still says NEEDS WORK, because the porch deck and steps are P4's and not built yet.

waste.what: Verifying the room in a temp copy: the room check reads the floor from the deck at y 2, which the fittings part (P4) has not built yet, so I wrote a throwaway script that adds the deck and steps to a copy of build.nbt before running the check.
waste.cost: one script, one extra make and check cycle (about 2 minutes)
waste.tool: room check or plan should take a flag such as --assume-deck (or read the porch deck from plan.md's porch_run spec) so a room can be checked before the porch part is merged

waste.what: Writing the layers() legend and three layers by hand for a 10 x 3 porch, with the cell-by-cell counting of the character columns.
waste.cost: about 4 minutes of drafting and recounting cells
waste.tool: plan.md-driven plan output that already includes the furniture-free grid as an editable layers() block, or a plan --draw flag printing the x-mod-10 ruler for the full width of the room

waste.what: Trying to place a hanging lantern under the porch beam: I had to fall back to standing lanterns on fence posts because nothing is built at y 6 yet, and I only found this by reading the room light map.
waste.tool: room check should report which cells lack a ceiling block (the hanging_lantern spot), so the hanging option can be chosen before building
